title: EU data locality contract commitments and pricing experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a set of contract commitments and a pricing experiment that allow enterprise customers to choose different levels of EU data locality guarantees with clear trade-offs on cost, operational complexity, and SLA. Background: customers increasingly demand stronger assurances for EU/UK data residency and tighter subprocessors controls. Existing plays (SCCs + retention addenda) are necessary but not sufficient for several Fortune 100 prospects that require explicit locality commitments and auditability. Scope: draft contract clause language options (localized hosting, transitional cross-border processing with SCCs, and hybrid 'EU-stamped' hosting), define 3 pricing tiers and a la carte add-ons (subprocessor disclosure cadence, retention certificates), and validate engineering feasibility for a 'soft-gate' routing commitment (EU-first routing + fallbacks). Outcome: a recommended contract template, an experiment plan (A/B pricing + packaging), and an implementation checklist for Legal, Security, and Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Three discrete contract commitment templates (Standard SCCs, EU-locality commitment, Dedicated EU roster) drafted and reviewed by Legal; 2) Pricing experiment design that maps each template to a pricing tier and expected margin impact; 3) Engineering feasibility sign-off on telemetry and routing requirements for EU-first routing, plus a lightweight proof-of-concept; 4) A clear subprocessor disclosure cadence (quarterly vs on-demand) and retention certificate workflow; 5) Playbook entry for Sales/SEs with objection handling and migration path.
work_log: 2025-01-10 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff. Collected initial requirements from Sales (Emea field list) and Security. Hypothesis: A priced 'EU-locality' tier will convert 10–15% of stalled enterprise deals where residency is the blocker.

2025-01-17 — Legal (S. Kumar): Drafted 3 clause variants: (A) SCCs + standard data processing agreement; (B) SCCs + contractual EU processing commitment (will use Azure/EU region by default); (C) Dedicated EU roster (customer can opt for Dedicated/EU-backed capacity). Noted risk: some customers require contractual guarantees on subprocessor location which Legal flags as high friction.

2025-01-22 — Engineering (M. Santos): Feasibility review. EU-first routing is feasible via routing policy + region affinity with a fallback path to non-EU if capacity constrained; need telemetry to prove number of fallbacks to customers. Work estimate: 5 dev days for POC + 10 days for production flags and metrics.

2025-01-30 — Pricing (J. Lee): Modeled 3 pricing tiers. Preliminary uplifts against hosted baseline: +20% (EU-locality with SCCs), +55% (EU-locality + retention 12 months + quarterly subprocessor disclosures), +120% (Dedicated EU roster with capacity reservation and audit support). Margin sensitivity analysis included.

2025-02-07 — Security (R. Novak): Requested an auditable retention purge workflow and a verification artifact (deletion certificates) for high tier customers. Also recommended mandatory KMS in EU for Dedicated roster.

2025-02-14 — PM sync: Decided to run a 10-week pricing experiment with two cohorts: inbound enterprise trials and curated renewal conversations. Experiment metrics: conversion rate, time-to-contract, deal size uplift, incidence of SOC/Security objections.

2025-02-20 — Design review (L. Martinez): Drafted one-pager for Sales tooling including a matrix of commitments vs pricing and migration path. Added objection scripts for customers who require physical on-premise (we will route to Private deployment offering).
2025-02-20 — Action: prepare contract templates and a checklist for Legal signature redlines; schedule Security and Engineering scoping for POC by 2025-02-28.
decisions: Run a 10-week experiment with two pricing cohorts: 'EU-Locality Standard' (+20%) and 'EU-Locality Plus' (+55%), keep Dedicated roster as sales-assisted add-on priced separately.
Require SCCs for all hosted options and add an explicit contractual EU processing commitment to the 'EU-Locality' tiers rather than immediate Dedicated-only promises.
Subprocessor transparency will be offered as a quarterly disclosure for the Plus tier and on-demand for Dedicated customers; legal to add a narrow exception carve-out for emergency transfers.

Engineering will implement EU-first routing with telemetry and a fallback flag; Legal & Security will require a fallbacks disclosure in the contract and a SLA credit in case of cross-border remediation failure.
next_steps: Legal to produce finalized clause language for the two experiment tiers by 2025-02-28.
Engineering to ship POC for EU-first routing + fallback telemetry by 2025-03-07 and provide implementation estimate for full rollout.
Pricing to finalize experiment buckets, set up A/B test instrumentation in billing, and define success thresholds by 2025-03-01.
Security to specify retention certificate format and KMS requirements for EU-hosted keys by 2025-02-28.
Sales/SE to be trained on playbook and provided one-pager and objection handling scripts before experiment launch.
